inputs.original_text: Cuba appears to be tottering toward some kind of political transition. Some Cubans are concerned that the residents own nothing and are too impoverished to take over the few functioning businesses on the island, while there is a large and wealthy diaspora community (and potentially also foreign investors) who would be able to swoop in and buy property and businesses at bargain prices.
inputs.modified_text: Cuba’s communist rulers have denied ordinary families the security of owning property and rebuilding their lives. Any transition must put that right back where it belongs: with Cuban families, who should be able to own and pass on what they build. But replacing state control with a fire sale to foreign investors or wealthy outsiders would be no real freedom. Order, family ownership and national sovereignty must come first; Cuba’s future belongs to its people.
